topIssues.title: blob-archiver does not support /eth/v1/beacon/blobs/ endpoint, breaking beacon fallback
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The blob-archiver does not implement the `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/<slot>` endpoint, which is the current beacon API endpoint used by `op-node` and `op-supernode` for fetching blobs. It only serves the older `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/<slot>` endpoint.

When `L1BeaconClient` rotates to the blob-archiver as a fallback (via `--l1.beacon-archiver`), the client calls `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/` which doesn't exist on the archiver — the request hits an unregistered route and returns a malformed response (bare JSON array instead of `{"data": [...]}`).

This affects both **op-node** and **op-supernode** since they share the same `BeaconHTTPClient`.

## Endpoint Support Matrix

| Endpoint | Beacon Proxy | Blob Archiver | QuickNode |
|----------|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/` (current) | works | **not implemented** | works |
| `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/` (old) | works | works | works |

## Root Cause

The beacon API transitioned from `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/` to `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/`. The op-node client was updated to use the new `/blobs/` endpoint ([op-service/sources/l1_beacon_client.go](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-service/sources/l1_beacon_client.go#L28)), but the blob-archiver was never updated to serve it.

In the [blob-archiver source](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/blob-archiver/blob/master/api/service/api.go#L109), only the old endpoint is registered:
```go
r.Get("/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{id}", result.blobSidecarHandler)
// missing: r.Get("/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{id}", result.blobsHandler)
```

## Response Format Differences

The two endpoints return different response formats:

**`/blobs/` (current)** — returns raw blobs:
```json
{"data": ["0x<hex blob>", "0x<hex blob>", ...]}
```

**`/blob_sidecars/` (old)** — returns sidecar objects:
```json
{"data": [{"index": "0", "blob": "0x...", "kzg_commitment": "0x...", ...}]}
```

The client deserializes into `APIBeaconBlobsResponse{Data []*Blob}` which expects the `/blobs/` format.

## Impact

- `--l1.beacon-archiver` / `--l1.beacon-fallbacks` is broken when pointing to the blob-archiver
- Only affects cases where the primary beacon can't serve blobs (e.g. PeerDAS nodes for old slots, expired blobs)
- Discovered during supernode canary testing on interop-v0

## Fix

The blob-archiver needs to add a handler for `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{id}` that returns the raw blob format `{"data": ["0x...", ...]}`.

topPRs.title: Chore/public docs migration
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
**Description**
Migrates all content from ethereum-optimism/docs into the monorepo at docs/public-docs/. This is a verbatim move with no content edits — Mintlify remains the docs framework, just pointed at the new location. The live site at docs.optimism.io and all 500+ redirects remain unchanged. After this PR merges, we'll do the Mintlify dashboard cutover, triage open issues/PRs in the old repo, and archive ethereum-optimism/docs.

**Tests**
No automated tests for this change. Correctness will be verified manually after the Mintlify dashboard cutover by confirming docs.optimism.io resolves correctly and spot-checking a sample of redirects.

**Additional context**
This consolidation means doc updates and their corresponding code changes can be reviewed atomically in a single PR, rather than requiring separate PRs across two repos. It also places docs directly alongside the code they describe, making it easier to catch and fix stale documentation. The existing docs/ directory (audits, postmortems) is untouched.

topPRs.title: feat: new zk dispute game
topPRs.author: 0xChin
topPRs.body:
## Summary

   Replaces `OptimisticZkGame` with a spec-compliant `ZKDisputeGame` that integrates into the OP Stack dispute infrastructure as game type `10`. This PR implements the full game lifecycle (create → challenge →
   prove → resolve → close) with permissionless access, DelayedWETH bond custody, and parent-chaining validation.

   ### Key changes

   **Architecture**
   - Renamed `OptimisticZkGame` → `ZKDisputeGame` with MCP clone (CWIA) pattern — all per-chain config injected via `gameArgs`, no constructor immutables
   - Deleted `AccessManager.sol` and `ISP1Verifier.sol` — fully permissionless design per spec
   - New generic `IZKVerifier` interface with 3-arg signature (`programId`, `publicValues`, `proof`) + `ISemver`, moved to `interfaces/dispute/zk/`

   **Lifecycle & Safety**
   - `initialize()`: parent validation (blacklist, retirement, game type match, anchor seq num strictly above, CHALLENGER_WINS rejection)
   - `challenge()`: `gameOver()` check first, single-challenge enforcement, bond deposited to DelayedWETH
   - `prove()`: guards for already-resolved games and parent CHALLENGER_WINS (defense-in-depth)
   - `resolve()`: cascading invalidity from parent, full bond distribution matrix per spec
   - `closeGame()`: pause gate, finality delay enforcement via ASR, NORMAL/REFUND mode determination
   - `claimCredit()`: two-phase DelayedWETH withdrawal (unlock → withdraw), no-op for zero-credit recipients

   **Storage optimization**
   - `ClaimData` struct packed from 4 slots → 3 slots (parentIndex + status + challenger in slot 1)
   - Renamed `counteredBy` → `challenger` for clarity

   **Bond distribution** (all scenarios from spec)
   - Unchallenged → proposer recovers initBond
   - Challenged, no proof → challenger gets initBond + challengerBond
   - Challenged, proof, prover == proposer → proposer gets all
   - Challenged, proof, prover != proposer → proposer gets initBond, prover gets challengerBond
   - Parent CHALLENGER_WINS → challenger gets all (or burned if unchallenged)
   - REFUND mode → original depositors get their bonds back

topPRs.title: fix(op-node): carry attributes in deposits-only request event
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Makes `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent` self-contained by carrying the original `AttributesWithParent`, eliminating the race condition where a pipeline reset clears `lastAttribs` between `BuildStartEvent` and `PayloadProcessEvent`.

This is an alternative to #19417 which changes `CriticalErrorEvent` to `ResetEvent`. That fix papers over the race by retrying; this fix eliminates the root cause by removing the dependence on mutable pipeline state.

### What changed

- `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent` now carries an `Attributes` field
- `EngineController` stores attributes from `BuildStartEvent` in `lastBuildAttribs` (survives pipeline resets)
- All emit sites pass attributes through: `build_invalid.go` uses `ev.Attributes` directly, `payload_process.go` uses `e.lastBuildAttribs`
- New `ApplyDepositsOnly` method on `AttributesQueue`/`DerivationPipeline` accepts provided attributes, flushes channels, and returns deposits-only version — without reading `lastAttribs`
- Missing or mismatched attributes is a `CriticalErrorEvent` — no fallback

### Emit site verification

There is exactly one place the event is constructed: `emitDepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequest`. All three call sites go through it:

1. **`build_invalid.go:47`** — passes `ev.Attributes` directly from `BuildInvalidEvent`. Always correct — same build cycle.
2. **`payload_process.go:46`** — SuperAuthority deny path. Passes `e.lastBuildAttribs`.
3. **`payload_process.go:65`** — Holocene `ExecutionInvalid`. Passes `e.lastBuildAttribs`.

### Staleness analysis for `lastBuildAttribs`

`lastBuildAttribs` is set in `onBuildStart` and read in `onPayloadProcess`. Could a second `BuildStartEvent` overwrite it before the first build's `PayloadProcessEvent` fires?

**The `AttributesHandler` prevents concurrent builds.** Its `sentAttributes` flag (set `true` before emitting `BuildStartEvent`, checked at line 167) prevents emitting a second `BuildStartEvent` while one is in flight. The flag is only cleared on reset, temporary error, or when attributes are consumed.

**After a reset, stale builds fail at the EL.** If a `ResetEvent` interleaves and eventually produces a new `BuildStartEvent` (overwriting `lastBuildAttribs`), the stale build's `BuildSealEvent` calls `engine.GetPayload` — but `forceReset` has already changed the EL's forkchoice via `tryUpdateEngine`, invalidating the old payload ID. The EL returns `UnknownPayload`, producing `PayloadSealExpiredErrorEvent` instead of `PayloadProcessEvent`. The deny check never fires for the stale build.

**Defense-in-depth validation catches any remaining edge case.** Both `emitDepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequest` and the handler in `PipelineDeriver` validate that the carried attributes match the event's `Parent` and `DerivedFrom`. If `lastBuildAttribs` is stale (wrong parent or derivation origin), the mismatch check fires a `CriticalErrorEvent` rather than silently using wrong attributes. This prevents incorrect derivation.

### Why the race exists

Events are queued, not inline. Between `BuildStartEvent` (which queues `ForkchoiceUpdateEvent` + `BuildStartedEvent`) and `PayloadProcessEvent` (where the deny check fires), a `ResetEvent` can interleave and clear `lastAttribs` on the `AttributesQueue`. The deny check then emits `DepositsOnlyPayloadAttributesRequestEvent`, whose handler previously read `lastAttribs` — which was nil.

The `EngineController`'s `lastBuildAttribs` field survives pipeline resets (only the pipeline's internal `AttributesQueue.lastAttribs` is cleared), bridging the gap.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests: `TestApplyDepositsOnly_WithNilLastAttribs` and `TestApplyDepositsOnly_PreservesParentAndDerivedFrom`
- [x] Updated `TestSuperAuthority/DeniedPayload_EmitsDepositsOnlyRequest` to set `lastBuildAttribs`
- [x] All `derive`, `engine`, and `attributes` tests pass
- [x] Full `op-node` build succeeds
- [ ] Should be validated with the supernode interop reorg acceptance tests from #19346

- Ported all targets from the three Makefiles under `rust/op-reth/` to justfiles, following the same deprecation shim pattern used by Go packages
- **`rust/op-reth/justfile`**: expanded with all targets from the Makefile — build, install, cross-compilation (via parameterized `build-cross`/`build-native` recipes), docker build+push, lint (fmt, clippy, typos, toml), test, profiling, and release tarball creation

- All three original Makefiles replaced with deprecation shims that list targets and include `justfiles/deprecated.mk` to print warnings and forward to `just`
- Updated `.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml` to use `just test-e2e-sysgo` instead of `make test-e2e-sysgo`
